live page unavailable — showing extracted text
Today we are splitting ⁦Ghostty's⁩ core into a library. The app you run keeps its window, its fonts and its configuration; the terminal underneath becomes something another program can embed.
A host hands libghostty a native surface and a size, and gets back a grid of cells it can draw however it likes. Input arrives as an event queue, not as callbacks into the ⁦host's⁩ event loop.
What does: everything that used to assume it owned a window.
An event queue instead of callbacks is the whole design in one sentence.
The ABI is versioned by struct size, so an embedder built against an older header keeps working until it asks for a field that did not exist yet.
I have wanted this for years. Every terminal library I have tried eventually grows its own opinion about how a window should look.
